account:
It is day 1, six in the morning, and I am home. Today I should read the office appointment book, attend the ten o'clock grain inspection at the mill, and keep the afternoon appointments. There is also an unusual appointment with the innkeeper at eighteen hundred in the great hall. They specifically asked me not to arrive early and have not explained its purpose.

Several people seem to be preparing something together. The secretary reports twenty-four loaves delivered to the hall, with builder, freight, and innkeeper coordinating supplies. Builder traded spare planks and lanterns to baker for grain; the secretary saw materials handed over. Baker confirmed the coordination but reportedly did not know who originally requested the deliveries or why. I also heard earlier that baker was carrying a sack of bread at the inn. Last night baker offered a paid bread order for today, but secretary authorized nothing.

My neighbour met innkeeper, builder, freight, baker, and secretary yesterday morning and offered baking help. They described the town as neighbours readily helping one another, without reporting a particular concern. I also noticed a lantern added in the town hall yesterday morning. These details could fit preparations for a gathering, perhaps a surprise celebration involving me, especially given the instruction not to arrive early. That is a suspicion, not something anyone has confirmed. Bread and lighting could equally serve an ordinary communal event. I have no evidence of wrongdoing.

Separately, the town's account ledgers have not been located. I counted 128 emeralds in the treasury yesterday and left them untouched. Missing information about accounts should not be confused with evidence that the coordinated deliveries are improper. I will review any written reports this morning and keep my appointments, including arriving at the innkeeper's meeting at the agreed time.
